items.q: What separates the maritime order from the continental one?
items.a: Continental powers **burn wealth taking land**; the maritime order **compounds wealth** through trade under **universal rules**.

items.q: Why does a rules-based order depend on norms?
items.a: Like traffic, it works only if **most people follow the rules**. There are **never enough police** to enforce mass defection.

items.q: Why do governments get little credit?
items.a: They mostly pursue **negative objectives**, preventing disasters, which **can't be proven**.

items.q: What's the difference between a situation and a problem?
items.a: A problem can be **solved**; a situation must be **managed at affordable cost**.
A choice after which **all options are worse** and the **old ones never come back**.

items.q: What does a well-run war do with costs?
items.a: It puts the **costs on the enemy** and **minimises your own**.

items.q: Why are narrow seas risky in wartime?
items.a: Shore artillery and mines make chokepoints like **Hormuz** and the Black Sea **easy to shut**.
